subject: Runway scenarios & QBR asks — GPU economics, batching & caching
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan@acme.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runway scenarios & QBR asks — GPU economics, batching & caching

Team / Rohan — attaching an initial runway spreadsheet with three scenarios for the upcoming QBR and a short summary below. This is intended for the leadership check-in tomorrow and to align on the ask we send to Acme for procurement planning. [Attachment: 2027-04-01-runway-scenarios-v1.xlsx]

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We modeled Conservative / Base / Aggressive demand through Q3 (tokens/day and concurrent sessions).
- Key levers: reserved GPUs vs. burst, batching aggressiveness, prefix caching hit-rate improvements.
- Primary metric for finance: marginal cost per 1M tokens served (USD). Secondary: p95 tail latency SLA (ms) and GPU utilization.

Quick numbers (base assumptions in sheet):
- Conservative: 40k tokens/sec peak, 220 GPUs reserved, avg util 52%, unit cost ~ $18 per 1M tokens.
- Base: 75k tokens/sec peak, 420 GPUs reserved (plus 100 burst), avg util 67%, unit cost ~ $11 per 1M tokens.
- Aggressive: 140k tokens/sec peak, 680 GPUs reserved (plus 300 burst), avg util 74%, unit cost ~ $8.5 per 1M tokens (assumes effective caching improvements).

Notes on batching & caching:
- Batching: moving from conservative batching (window=5ms) to aggressive batching (window=20ms) increases throughput but risks 60–120ms added latency on short requests. We show p95 impact per scenario.
- Prefix/KV caching: a 10–20% effective cache hit rate on warm prefixes reduces overall token throughput by ~9–16% in the model — big lever to reduce reserved commit.

Asks / decisions needed before the QBR: 
1) Leadership commitment: target scenario to present (Conservative|Base|Aggressive).
2) Tradeoff: Acceptable p95 SLA delta (we need to know if +30–50ms at p95 is tolerable for this customer class).
3) Procurement ask: if we present Base, procurement should prepare an initial reserved commit of 420 GPUs with 100-burst option for 6 months.

Rohan — can you confirm whether Acme would accept a 150ms p95 for batch-heavy workflows? If not, tell us which product paths we must prioritize (latency vs cost).

Next steps: I’ll update the sheet with any leadership changes and circulate a short one-pager for the QBR deck by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kernel-selection-and-batching-notes.pdf]

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@acme.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway scenarios & QBR asks — GPU economics, batching & caching

Thanks Kimberly — received and useful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- For our knowledge tasks (short responses, avg 18 tokens output), p95 is the priority. We cannot tolerate >130ms for those flows.
- For long-form generation (batch jobs), we can accept higher p95 if cost delta is meaningful.

Can you split the numbers in the sheet by "short-response" vs "long-form" traffic? That will help procurement justify a blended approach.

I’ll loop procurement and our platform lead to review the Base scenario.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Platform — Acme AI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runway scenarios & QBR asks — GPU economics, batching & caching

Kimberly + Lauren — I took a pass on the workbook and added a "traffic mix" tab that separates short-response vs long-form across scenarios. High level notes below (see inline comments in sheet):

- If Acme insists on <=130ms p95 for short-response, our recommended plan is: maintain reserved profile aligned to Base but tighten batching windows for low-latency routes (per-route override). That pushes Base unit cost ~ +9% (from $11 to ~$12 per 1M) but keeps short-response p95 in range.
- Caching: engineering estimates 12% effective hit-rate for warm prefixes within 6 weeks of deployment if we prioritize a small KV-store rollout. That reduces required reserved GPUs for Base by ~30–35 GPUs.
- Burst sizing: the 100-burst option is OK, but with expected spike profiles we should increase transient capacity throttles (auto-scale faster) to avoid tail incidents. Ops already has a runbook draft.

Action items for leadership decision:
A) Approve Base + per-route latency overrides (recommended) — this is my pick.
B) Approve small KV roll (6-week dev) to capture caching benefits — combined finance/eng ask ~ $95k one-time infra + dev allocation.
C) Approve procurement ask (420 reserved + 100 burst) conditioned on A/B being true.

Lauren — can you comment on whether this messaged approach is acceptable to present in the QBR deck? I can draft a single slide showing cost vs. p95 tradeoff.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Revenue Engineering — Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick update and confirmed action list after reading Rishi’s changes and Rohan’s constraints:

Decisions: 
- Present the Base scenario in the QBR.
- Commit to per-route latency overrides for short-response workflows (keeps p95 <=130ms).
- Approve a small KV caching pilot (6 weeks) — finance/eng ask will be sent to ops for budget.

Procurement ask (to Acme and our GTM lead): we will request 420 reserved GPUs + 100-burst for an initial 6-month term. Procurement, please prepare a starter SOW referencing ~420 reserved units with monthly billing; include a clause for 30% reduction if KV pilot shows expected gains within 6 weeks.

Rishi / Lauren / Vivek — please review the updated slide I attached and flag any wording changes by EOD Monday. I will finalize the one-pager for the QBR and post the deck link to the Drive folder. [Attachment: 2027-04-01-runway-scenarios-v1.xlsx]

Thanks everyone — nice progress.

Kimberly Park
